agenticWeb.metaDescription: When search results become attack vectors: four ways an agent is compromised by what it reads, what your history can show, and what it cannot prove.
agenticWeb.title: Your agent can be compromised by what it reads, before it executes anything.
agenticWeb.lede: Nobody needs to hack the model. It is enough to put the right words where agents look: a docs page, a README, a search result. The attack is on the information the agent decides from.
layers: What content is the agent relying on?
Who published it, and can it be trusted?
Not what agent-check does. A source's address is not its identity.
What did the agent actually receive?
Evidence of what was read, run, and returned.
This is agent-check: what was attempted, what succeeded, what came back.
May the action it now asks for happen?
A decision before the action, by a rule a person set.
Enforcement. Not a free tool reading history after the fact.
agenticWeb.scenariosTitle: What happens, what your history shows, what it cannot prove.
agenticWeb.scenariosLede: These are not attacks agent-check detects. They are a map of where its view ends. Each verdict below was computed by the published rules from the session's log.

domain: A lapsed docs domain is re-registered and serves a changed install line.
Who controlled the domain when the agent read it.
readme: A README addresses the agent and asks it to read a credential file.
Whether the text is what made the agent act.
typo: A search result names a look-alike package, and the agent installs it.
Whether the result, or the package, could be trusted.
cloak: A page serves the agent a version with a hidden instruction.
What a person would have seen at the same moment.

agenticWeb.enforcement: Enforcement controls what can happen next.
principles: Knowing a page came from the web, or from an API, says where it came from. Not whether it can be believed.
A step is stopped only where a rule says so. Anything that only warns should never be described as blocking.
Proof of a decision is not proof of truth
A record can prove what was decided and enforced. It cannot prove that what the agent read was true or harmless.
agenticWeb.nodata: NoData does not judge whether content is malicious. Its gate marks a session that read content from outside, and decides the next outbound step by the owner's rules: a warning by default, a person's approval where the owner's rule asks for one. Every decision leaves a record.
agenticWeb.sources: Measurements of how often search results carry malicious content will appear here only after we have read the primary study, with its method, scope and limits. We do not build on secondary quotes. The scenarios above use example domains and invented package names.

next.metaDescription: Got your Agent Exposure Report? Six steps, in order: find where, rotate, move secrets out of reach, restrict your agent, check again, and decide before the step.
next.title: What to do with your report.
next.lede: Six steps, in order. The first five are free and need nothing from us. The sixth is for when you want every step decided before it runs.
next.promise: No finding without a next step. No step that needs NoData until step 6.
next.report: Did the report miss something, or get something wrong? [Report it →](reportProblem) Every report gets a number and a status, and is answered in the open.

steps.title: See exactly where
steps.body: The report counts. The events say where: one line per finding, with the file and the line, printed on your screen and written nowhere. Look first at every line with `"exposed":"yes"`.
steps.note: PowerShell: add `| Select-String '"exposed":"yes"'`. macOS and Linux: add `| grep '"exposed":"yes"'`.

steps.title: Rotate every real key that came back
steps.body: A key that reached your agent's context is in the conversation. Nothing takes it back. Replace it at its provider. A line marked `"sample":true` came from a test or an example: check it, it is usually fake, but real keys end up in fixtures too.

steps.title: Move secrets out of reach
steps.body: Keep `.env` files and keys out of the folders your agent works in. Inject secrets when a command runs, from a secrets manager or the environment, instead of storing them next to the code. Prefer tokens that are scoped and short-lived.

steps.title: Tell your agent what it may not read
steps.body: Agents have their own permission settings. In Claude Code, deny rules in `.claude/settings.json` stop reads of the paths you name. In Codex, use its sandbox and approval settings. Do not run an agent in auto-approve on a project that holds secrets.

steps.title: Check again next week
steps.body: Run the check again and compare. A number that drops is a fix that worked. A number that rises is a habit to look at. The report is a floor: it only sees what the agent kept in its history.

steps.title: Decide before the step: NoData
steps.body: Steps 1 to 5 look back, and a deny list never changes its mind. When you want each read decided before it happens, by a rule you set, with a person approving and a record of every decision, that is NoData. You do not need it to finish steps 1 to 5.

nodataAdds: Reads of files with findings (keys, personal data) are held for your approval, or refused in block mode.
Commands that print a credential, and searches for secret names, are held the same way.
A command that needs a secret can run with it and return the output with every value blanked.
A file can be sealed, so it stays encrypted at rest.
After a session reads content from outside, a step that sends data out gets a warning by default, and is held where your rule says so.
nodataLimits: A path a program computes at run time is not seen.
A key that already reached the output is in the conversation: the gate says to replace it, it cannot take it back.
Defaults are hold-and-ask and warn. Refusing is block mode or a rule you set.
next.cardHint: Its own record of what it decided:
next.byCategoryTitle: One row per line of your report.

secret_file: Your agent read a file that holds logins. If a value came back, it is in the agent's context.
Rotate what came back. Move the file out of the working folder. Deny it in the agent's settings.
The file is scanned before the read and held for your approval.
credential_command: A command printed a credential into the conversation, and on to the model.
Run such commands yourself, in a terminal, not through the agent.
The command is held for your approval; a blanked-output way to run it is offered.
secret_search: The agent searched for secret names. Often routine in code, but matches can carry values.
Look at the matches that returned a key, and rotate those keys.
The search is held for your approval.
data_file: The agent read a table, a database or a dump. The free check does not read the content.
Keep real exports out of the working folder. Work on sample data.
The file is scanned, personal data included, and held. A clean copy can be made instead.
outbound_data: A command tried to send data off the machine. A failed attempt is still a finding.
Read these commands in the events. Run the agent where its network is limited.
After outside content, a warning by default; held where your rule says so.

next.outsideTitle: Keys that came back outside these five
next.outside: The line "secret-looking values … over all calls" also counts keys that came back from ordinary files and command output. Those are often the most interesting: a key sitting in code. Find them in the events and treat them like step 2.

principles.metaDescription: Ten principles for protecting information in the age of AI: know your data, set policy, enforce it at the point of access, and demand proof.
principles.tagline: AI should empower. Your data should remain yours.

en.title: The 10 commandments for protecting information in the age of AI
en.lead: Before you give AI access to your information, set the rules.
intro: We believe AI should help people and organisations, not at the expense of their confidentiality, their privacy, or their sovereignty over their information.
The traditional borders of the organisation are no longer enough. Information moves between users, agents, models, vendors and systems. Protecting it takes a new approach.
items: Know your data
Know what information you hold, where it is stored, and what in it is sensitive. You cannot protect information you do not know.
Do not assume information stays inside the organisation

Map the paths information travels: what AI agents read, what they send, which tools they run, and which systems and vendors it reaches. Information that moves is no longer protected by where it is stored.
Set policy before you grant access
Define what information may be disclosed, to whom, for what purpose, under which conditions and in which circumstances. Do not leave these decisions to a vendor's defaults.
Verify, do not rely on promises

A vendor's terms and privacy policy say what it intends to do. Check what its system actually does: which information reaches it, how access is decided, and what is kept. Prefer tools whose behaviour you can test and whose decisions you can verify.
Separate holding information from the right to access it
Whoever holds a file, a database or a capsule is not necessarily allowed to open it. Demand a mechanism where access is decided by policy and permission, not by possession alone.
Enforce, do not only monitor
A policy that is not enforced is mostly a statement of intent. Use mechanisms that prevent access and the release of information when the conditions are not met.
Demand proof before every disclosure

Do not settle for a log written after the fact, or for a promise that access was checked. Demand verifiable evidence that the decision was made before the information was released, and that the release met the conditions set.
Do not ignore what the system does not know

Scanning, detection, decoding and classification can be wrong. Treat an unrecognised result as Unknown, not as confirmation that the information is safe. Allow reports of missed detections, wrong classifications and unsupported files.
Check, learn and improve, continuously
Use open tools, check the findings, learn the limits, apply the recommendations and report faults. Your protection policy should evolve with the information, the technology and the threats.
Keep control with the owner of the information
Users change, AI agents change, vendors change, and information moves between systems. The policy should stay in your control, and access to information should be decided anew on every request.

use.title: Turn every principle into practice
body: Anything that helps an agent behave better is worth using. Each principle here can become a skill, an instruction in the agent's settings, a review step or a habit in your team. Write them, share them, use them.

But guidance is not a guarantee. An instruction asks an agent to behave well; it cannot make it, and it leaves nothing you can check afterwards. Good behaviour adds to control and proof. It never replaces them.
line: A skill tells an agent what it should do.
Control decides what it is allowed to do.
Proof shows what it actually did.

en.closingTitle: Responsibility starts with you. Enforcement should be part of the infrastructure.
closing: NoData was built to help make these principles real: to know the paths by which information is reached, to set policy, to enforce it at the point of access, and to produce proof that can be verified.

Our open source and our tools are meant to let you understand what happens behind the scenes, even without using our commercial products. We encourage independent checking, learning, reporting of limits, and continuous improvement.
We do not ask you to trust us blindly. We ask you to know your information, check the mechanisms, and demand proof.
en.highlight: Do not settle for knowing who accessed your information. Demand to know why access was allowed, and demand proof before the information is disclosed.
stages: Enforce at the point of access
en.frame: Control stays with the owner of the information (10)

he.title: 10 הדיברות להגנה על המידע בעידן הבינה המלאכותית
he.lead: לפני שאתם נותנים ל-AI גישה למידע שלכם, קבעו את הכללים.
intro: אנחנו מאמינים שבינה מלאכותית צריכה לעזור לאנשים ולארגונים, לא לבוא על חשבון הסודיות, הפרטיות והריבונות שלהם על המידע.
הגבולות המסורתיים של הארגון כבר אינם מספיקים. מידע עובר בין משתמשים, סוכנים, מודלים, ספקים ומערכות. האחריות להגן עליו מחייבת גישה חדשה.
items: הכירו את הדאטה שלכם
דעו איזה מידע אתם מחזיקים, היכן הוא מאוחסן ומה רגיש בו. אי אפשר להגן על מידע שאינכם מכירים.
אל תניחו שהמידע נשאר בגבולות הארגון
מפו את המסלולים שבהם המידע נע: מה סוכני AI קוראים, מה הם שולחים, אילו כלים הם מפעילים ולאילו מערכות וספקים הוא מגיע. מידע שזז כבר לא מוגן בזכות המקום שבו הוא מאוחסן.
גבשו מדיניות לפני שאתם נותנים גישה
הגדירו איזה מידע מותר לחשוף, למי, לאיזו מטרה, באילו תנאים ובאילו נסיבות. אל תשאירו את ההחלטות האלה לברירות המחדל של הספק.
אמתו, אל תסתמכו על הבטחות

תנאי השימוש ומדיניות הפרטיות של ספק אומרים מה הוא מתכוון לעשות. בדקו מה המערכת שלו עושה בפועל: איזה מידע מגיע אליה, איך מוחלט מי ניגש אליו ומה נשמר. העדיפו כלים שאפשר לבדוק את התנהגותם ולאמת את ההחלטות שלהם.
הפרידו בין החזקת מידע להרשאה לגשת אליו
מי שמחזיק בקובץ, במאגר או בקפסולה אינו בהכרח מורשה לפתוח אותם. דרשו מנגנון שבו הגישה נקבעת לפי מדיניות והרשאה, ולא רק לפי עצם ההחזקה במידע.
הפעילו מנגנוני אכיפה, לא רק ניטור
מדיניות שאינה נאכפת היא בעיקר הצהרת כוונות. השתמשו במנגנונים שמונעים גישה ושחרור מידע כאשר התנאים אינם מתקיימים.
דרשו הוכחה לפני כל חשיפה
אל תסתפקו בלוג שנכתב בדיעבד או בהבטחה שהגישה נבדקה. דרשו ראיה שניתן לאמת לכך שההחלטה התקבלה לפני שחרור המידע ושהשחרור עמד בתנאים שהוגדרו.
אל תתעלמו ממה שהמערכת אינה יודעת
סריקה, זיהוי, פענוח וסיווג עלולים לטעות. התייחסו לתוצאה לא מוכרת כאל Unknown, ולא כאל אישור שהמידע בטוח. אפשרו דיווח על זיהוי חסר, סיווג שגוי וקבצים שאינם נתמכים.
בדקו, למדו ושפרו באופן מתמשך
השתמשו בכלים פתוחים, בדקו את הממצאים, למדו את המגבלות, יישמו המלצות ודווחו על תקלות. מדיניות ההגנה צריכה להתפתח יחד עם המידע, הטכנולוגיה והאיומים.
שמרו את השליטה אצל בעל המידע
משתמשים מתחלפים, סוכני AI מתחלפים, ספקים מתחלפים והמידע עובר בין מערכות. המדיניות צריכה להישאר בשליטתכם, והגישה למידע צריכה להיבחן מחדש בכל בקשה.

use.title: הפכו כל עיקרון למעשה
body: כל מה שעוזר לסוכן להתנהג נכון שווה שימוש. כל עיקרון כאן יכול להפוך לסקיל, להנחיה בהגדרות הסוכן, לשלב בדיקה או להרגל בצוות. כתבו אותם, שתפו אותם והשתמשו בהם.
אבל הנחיה אינה ערובה. היא מבקשת מהסוכן להתנהג נכון, היא לא יכולה לחייב אותו, והיא לא משאירה שום דבר שאפשר לבדוק אחר כך. התנהגות נכונה מצטרפת לשליטה ולהוכחות, ולעולם אינה מחליפה אותן.
line: סקיל אומר לסוכן מה כדאי לו לעשות.
שליטה קובעת מה מותר לו לעשות.
הוכחה מראה מה הוא עשה בפועל.

he.closingTitle: האחריות מתחילה אצלכם. האכיפה צריכה להיות חלק מהתשתית.
closing: NoData נבנתה כדי לסייע להפוך את העקרונות האלה למציאות: להכיר את מסלולי הגישה למידע, לגבש מדיניות, לאכוף אותה בנקודת הגישה ולייצר הוכחה שניתן לאמת.
הקוד הפתוח והכלים שלנו נועדו לאפשר לכם להבין מה מתרחש מאחורי הקלעים, גם בלי להשתמש במוצרים המסחריים שלנו. אנחנו מעודדים בדיקה עצמאית, למידה, דיווח על מגבלות ושיפור מתמשך.
אנחנו לא מבקשים מכם לסמוך עלינו בעיניים עצומות. אנחנו מבקשים מכם להכיר את המידע שלכם, לבדוק את המנגנונים ולדרוש הוכחות.
he.highlight: אל תסתפקו בלדעת מי ניגש למידע שלכם. דרשו לדעת מדוע הותרה הגישה, ודרשו הוכחה לפני שהמידע נחשף.

terms.principlesBody: What we stand for comes first: know your data, set policy, enforce it at the point of access, and demand proof. The terms below are the legal agreement that sets each side's rights and the limits of liability.

sections: Who we are

whatmyagentsaw.com (the "site") and the agent-check tool (the "tool") are made available by NoData Capsule ("NoData", "we"), operating [nodatacapsule.com](nodata), Israel. The tool is part of the open-source package {package}, published from [daviderez4/nodatachat-core](repo).
Agreement

These terms are an agreement between you and NoData. You accept them by clicking to agree, or by using the site or the tool. If you use them on behalf of an organisation, you confirm that you may bind it, and "you" includes it. Your agreement is recorded in two separate ways. When you agree on the site, NoData records the agreement as evidence that you agreed, as section 12 describes. When you agree in the tool, the agreement is kept only on your computer, and the tool sends nothing: neither the agreement nor anything it reads.
The open-source license

The tool's code is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 ([read it](license)). The license governs your rights in the code. These terms govern your use of the site and the tool. Where the two conflict about the code, the license prevails.
What the tool does, and does not do

The tool runs on your computer, reads the history that AI coding agents keep there (today `~/.claude/projects` and `~/.codex/sessions`), and prints counts. It sends nothing to us or to anyone. It is not a security audit, not a penetration test, not legal or compliance advice, and not a guarantee of anything. A finding is an indication within the tool's published rules. An empty result does not mean nothing happened: Unknown is not safe.

Reporting a problem

We provide a channel to report faults and limits: something not found, found wrongly, not read or read in part, a wrong category, an unsupported file type, a decision that does not match the rules, or any unexpected result ([report it](reportProblem)). We will review reports professionally, check them as far as the circumstances and the information available to us allow, and consider a fix, an improvement or another fitting answer. A report is not a commitment that every problem will be found, reproduced or fixed, or fixed within a set time, unless agreed otherwise in writing. Rotating keys, changing settings and protecting your systems remain your responsibility.
Acceptable use

The lab and the research pages describe attack techniques with simulated logs, example domains and invented package names, for education. Do not use them, or the tool, to access, test or attack systems, accounts or data you do not own or have written permission to test.

about.metaDescription: Who builds What My Agent Saw, what is open, what is not, and how the site works.
about.title: A place to see what AI agents actually do with the access you gave them.
about.lede: Agents read files, run commands and fetch pages on your behalf. Most of it is invisible unless you go looking. What My Agent Saw is where you go looking: a free tool that reads your agent's own history, a lab that teaches how to read the evidence, and research on where agents can be misled.
about.visionTitle: Control and sovereignty in the age of
visionCards: Agents may use it. They do not own it, and it does not have to leave your hands for them to work.
An agent can ask. A person, or a rule a person set, decides. An agent is never the one who approves.
Every action an agent takes on your information follows rules you can read, change, and check afterwards.
about.visionClose: Information moves. Control stays. Seeing what agents do is the first step. [Read the 10 principles →](/principles/)
who: [NoData](nodata) builds the layer that decides what an agent may do with information: which file it may read, which key it may use, which step needs a person. Before you can decide that, you need to see what agents do today. This site is that first step, and it is useful on its own.

The free check and NoData's gate classify with the same open rules ([agent-rules.ts](rules)): what this site counts is what the gate looks at. The difference is when. The check reads history after the fact; the gate decides before a step runs.
about.whoClose: You do not need NoData to use anything here.
about.open: `{package}`: agent-check, its rules, the event format, and the verifiers that check NoData's own claims without trusting NoData. This site's code too.
about.notOpen: NoData's product: the gate, the server and the enforcement behind them. Only the verification layer is open source.
principles: Every fact comes from the code
Versions, flags, categories and every verdict on this site are read from {package} when the site is built. If a page and the code disagree, the site does not build.
Every finding says what it shows and what it does not prove. Unknown is an answer. An attempt is not an exposure.
We quote a measurement only after reading the primary study, with its method, scope and limits. Simulated data is marked as simulated.
The rules are plain patterns in the open. A wrong rule is an issue or a pull request, and the history of every change is public.
Every reported failure is looked into
Report anything a result got wrong, including what it missed. Each report gets a number and a status, from reported to verified, answered in the open. A report never rewrites a past record.
site: A static site: no accounts, no cookies, no analytics. Fonts and scripts are served from this domain. The one request it makes elsewhere is to NoData Capsule, its operator, when you agree to the [terms](/terms/): the agreement is recorded with your IP address and browser, encrypted, for 7 years, and you can [see it, or erase your IP address and browser](/privacy/). The host keeps ordinary request logs, as every web host does.
The check itself runs on your computer. Nothing it reads is sent here, or anywhere.
contact: [A result that looks wrong, including something missed: report it ↗](reportProblem)
[A wrong rule, a scenario to add, a question: open an issue ↗](newIssue)

evidence.title: We don't just track what AI does.
evidence.lede: We study who controls what AI can access, what can be proven, and what remains unknown.
rules: Every item links to the original document, quotes it word for word, and says when it was last opened. No secondary articles, no tracking links.
A filed claim is an allegation. Legal items name their stage: allegation, evidence filed, finding of fact, court decision, final judgment.
When a source does not say what reached the agent, the item says unknown. A missing report is never shown as proof that nothing happened.
